- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤ -0.33), model underestimates; adjust upward by 1–3% to reflect risk-off bias.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >5% from prior period), model often overshoots; cap forecast at +3% above prior peak for next 3–5 periods.
- If true outcome shows mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days below 65–70), model tends to lag; add 0.5–1.5% lag correction to forecast.
- For 30-day horizon, model often overreacts to short-term sentiment shifts; smooth 3–5 day moving average of sentiment before adjusting forecast.
- If sentiment history shows alternating bullish/bearish cycles, model fails to capture mean reversion; apply 1–2% downward bias if sentiment flips from + to - or vice versa.
